content.content:
# Resend — transactional email for Next.js Resend sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) through a small HTTP API with delivery logs, webhooks and domain verification. The official Node.js library `resend` wraps the whole Resend REST API, has typed responses and works in Node.js 18+, serverless and edge runtimes. ## Install ```bash npm install resend ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` RESEND_API_KEY=re_placeholder RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The API key is created in the Resend dashboard (API Keys). The From address must be on a domain you have verified in Resend, or `onboarding@resend.dev` while testing. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/resend.ts`: ```ts import { Resend } from "resend"; export const resend = new Resend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the API key to the browser. ## 3. Send an email ```ts import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; const { data, error } = await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Welcome!", html: "

Thanks for signing up.

", text: "Thanks for signing up.", }); ``` `data.id` is the message id; use it to look the email up in the dashboard logs. ## 4. Send with a React template Write the email as a React component and pass it with `react`; Resend renders it to HTML: ```tsx import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; import { PasswordResetEmail } from "@/emails/password-reset"; await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Reset your password", react: PasswordResetEmail({ name: "Ada", actionUrl: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }), }); ``` The `@react-email/components` package gives layout primitives for email clients; plain JSX works too. ## 5. Handle errors `emails.send` does not throw on a refused message: it resolves to `{ data: null, error }` with the error `name` and `message` from Resend (invalid API key, unverified domain, rate limit). Check `error` where the email is triggered so a failed email does not break the request that caused it. ## Why teams pick Resend - Built for developers: one API call to send, typed SDK, React templates in the codebase. - Delivery logs, bounces and webhooks live in the same dashboard as the API keys. - Domain verification with DKIM and SPF guided from the dashboard. # env files (can opt-in for committing if needed) .env* next-env.d.ts src: app lib src/app: dashboard favicon.ico globals.css layout.tsx page.tsx src/lib: users.ts

content.text:
Welcome and password reset emails are now wired into `src/lib/users.ts`, sent through Resend. Lint passes. `tsc` reports one error, in `src/app/layout.tsx` (`Cannot find name 'LayoutProps'`). I didn't touch that file, so it looks pre-existing. I haven't sent a real email, since that needs a real API key.

I picked Resend because `docs/resend.md` and `llms.txt` were already in the repo. It has a typed SDK and delivery logs, and it works in Next.js server code.

**What I added**
- **`src/lib/resend.ts`:** the Resend client, as in the docs.
- **`src/lib/email.ts`:** `sendWelcomeEmail` and `sendPasswordResetEmail`. They use plain HTML plus a text version, so there are no extra dependencies beyond `resend`. User names are HTML-escaped. A refused or failed send logs an error and returns `false` instead of throwing, so an email failure never breaks signup.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`:**
  - `createUser()` adds the user and sends the welcome email. There was no create function before, so I added one.
  - `requestPasswordReset(email)` emails a reset link that expires after 1 hour. It does nothing for unknown emails, so callers can't tell which addresses have accounts.
  - `consumePasswordResetToken(token)` is the check to use when the user opens the reset link. Each token works once.
- **`.env.example`:** placeholders for `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`.
- **`.gitignore`:** it ignored `.env*`, so I added `!.env.example` so the example file can be committed.

**Not done yet**
- Reset tokens live in memory, like the existing user array. They are lost on restart and won't work across serverless instances, so move them to a database along with the users.
- There is no `/reset-password` page or form that calls `consumePasswordResetToken`. The email links to `/reset-password?token=…`, so that page needs building. The app also has no password storage yet.
- Before sending to real addresses, verify your domain in Resend and set `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` to an address on it.
